B: Hello. Can you hear me all right?
A: Yeah, hello. I can hear you. Tomasz.
B: Neil. Good to meet you. This is the last one, I think.
A: Yeah, last one. Is going fast.
B: It is. Er, I'm guessing from the hi-vis on the chair that you're in a similar line of work to me. Or near it.
A: Ha. Yeah, I forgot it's there. I fit kitchens. Carpenter. I work for small company in Basingstoke.
B: Ah. I'm a site services manager at a packaging factory, so maintenance mostly. I spend a lot of my time managing contractors, people like you, and making sure they've signed in and done the risk assessment.
A: Oh, so you are the man with the clipboard.
B: I'm afraid I am. Though to be fair, I'm the one who reads the method statement properly. Most people just sign it.
A: Yeah, I just sign it. Sorry.
B: Ha. I won't hold it against you. Do you enjoy the work?
A: Yeah, I like it. The fitting part, I like. When the doors hang straight and the worktop sits nice to the wall, is good feeling. The paperwork, the timesheets, no. My boss is always chasing me. And the knees, they're not happy now. I'm forty-two, and I'm on the floor all day.
B: The knees are the thing. Our engineers say the same. Have you got proper kneepads?
A: I have, but sometimes I forget to put them. Is stupid, I know.
B: Well, I'll stop sounding like a health and safety manager. Where's home originally, if you don't mind me asking?
A: Poland. South-east, Podkarpackie. Near Rzeszów.
B: We went to Krakow a few years ago, my wife and I. Loved it. We did the salt mine at Wieliczka, which I'd wanted to see for years. I'm interested in old industrial places, mines especially. My dad worked at a pit.
A: Ah, Wieliczka is good, yeah. I went with school when I was kid. The chapel down there, all from salt.
B: The chandeliers as well. Extraordinary. And I liked Nowa Huta, which I don't think most tourists bother with.
A: Ha. No, most people don't go there. Is all concrete. But you like that, I think.
B: I do, yes. Julie was less convinced. What do you do when you're not fitting kitchens?
A: Fishing, carp. And I fix old bikes in the garage. For my son and his friends. I found one at the tip last month, it only needed new brakes. Now is like new.
B: That's funny, I've been meaning to get my bike serviced for about a year. It's been in the shed since my thirties, more or less.
A: You don't need service, maybe. Check the brake pads, the chain. If chain is rusty, new chain is cheap. Tyres, if they're cracked on the side, change them. Most things you can do yourself with YouTube.
B: That's encouraging. I'm fine with a soldering iron, but bikes I've always left to someone else.
A: Is easier than soldering, I think. Is all there, you can see it. Cables, you can see where is the problem.
B: Right. I'll give it a go before I pay anyone, then.
